sections.h2: Where is the Chippewa County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, MI 49783. The state treasury directory lists the phone as 906-635-6312, the fax as 906-635-6855 and the email as rod@chippewacountymi.gov. Call ahead for counter hours, since none are posted on the land records site.

Chippewa County is in the eastern Upper Peninsula, and Sault Ste. Marie is the county seat. A seller on Drummond Island, in the Sault, or anywhere along the St. Marys River records the deed here. Mail works as well as a visit, as long as the document, the fee and the return envelope go in together.

sections.h2: How is Chippewa County organized, and who answers tax questions?
sections.html:
Chippewa County government was set up in 1826 and once reached across most of what is now the Upper Peninsula and parts of Minnesota. The Act of March 9, 1843 cut that vast area down, and the county now follows the Canadian border along the St. Marys River. Sault Ste. Marie anchors the Sault Ste. Marie micropolitan area, and Drummond Island is part of the county.

The county itself operates the jail, maintains rural roads, runs the major local courts and keeps the deed and mortgage records. Police, fire, building and zoning, tax assessment and street maintenance belong to the cities and townships. A seller with a question about an assessed value or a building permit therefore calls the local township or city office, not the register of deeds. The register of deeds answers questions about what has been recorded against the parcel, and it can tell you whether an older mortgage was ever discharged on the record before your buyer's lender asks.

  • Recording, indexing and copies: the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street.
  • Assessment and local zoning: the city or township where the house sits.
  • Tax certificates for warranty-type deeds: the treasurer offices named in MCL 211.135.

sections.h2: Why does a Chippewa County house sale end at the Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Only a recording here puts the new deed into the county's land record. The office also holds the mortgages, discharges and liens that a title agent hunts for when clearing your title.

The online land records system shows how deep the file goes. Its indexes start on May 16, 1865, which gives a title examiner well over a century of names to search. Sellers who inherited a Chippewa County house can use that index to find the deed that put the family on title.

  • Guests search the index free of charge.
  • Members log in with a group, user ID and password, and login charges may apply.
  • PDF copies are bought by credit card after the search.

sections.h2: What do recording and copy charges look like in Chippewa County?
sections.html:
Under MCL 600.2567 the recording fee is $30.00 a document unless a charter county has adopted a different schedule. The same section prices copies at a dollar a page and certifying a recorded document at $5.00.

Chippewa County land record charges drawn from the statute and the online system
ServiceChargeWhere it comes from
Recording a document$30.00, any page countMCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Extra instrument on an assignment or discharge$3.00 eachMCL 600.2567(1)(b)
Certifying a recorded document$5.00MCL 600.2567(1)(d)
Online PDF copy$1.00 per pageChippewa land records site
Online order fee$5.00 per orderChippewa land records site

Five dollars of the $30.00 is set aside for the register of deeds' automation fund. Send payment together with the deed, because the office wants it at the time of filing.

sections.h2: Which Chippewa County deeds escape transfer tax?
sections.html:
MCL 207.505 carves out a list of instruments, and a few of them come up often here. A mortgage or other security instrument is carved out. So is a lease, and so is a deed whose stated consideration is under $100.

  • A deed where the grantor is the federal government, the state or a local government.
  • A deed given to settle, or in place of foreclosing, a government-backed or insured loan.
  • A corrective deed that repairs a defect in title the buyer already holds.
  • A boundary-straightening deed when no money changes hands.
  • A transfer between husband and wife that sets up or dissolves an entireties tenancy.

Everything else owes the county 55 cents and the state $3.75 for each $500 slice. Phone the office to learn which exemption, if any, fits your deed.

For a taxable sale, work it out on paper before closing. A house that sells at $161,900, the Census median value for the county, covers 324 slices of $500. County tax comes to $178.20 and state tax to $1,215.00, which makes $1,393.20 together. The deed has to show the full consideration, or an affidavit with the value goes on top of it, so the clerk can check your arithmetic.

sections.h2: What else must a Chippewa County deed carry besides the legal description?
sections.html:
MCL 565.201 requires details about the people named in the deed, and one missing item stops the recording. Every grantee's address must be printed, using the street number where street numbers are normal and a post office address where they are not.

Any Social Security number must have its first five digits removed or blacked out. A deed in a foreign language needs an English translation stapled on. Anything signed after January 1, 1964 must show who drafted it, with a business address. A notary's printed name belongs on the same page as the notary's signature.

sections.h2: Do I need a tax certificate to record a Chippewa County deed?
sections.html:
For most warranty-type deeds, yes. MCL 211.135 directs the office to demand certification that no taxes are unpaid for the five years preceding the deed, together with a statement of any liens or tax titles on the parcel.

Certificates come from the county treasurer and from the treasurer of the local city, village or township. Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds are among the exceptions. Skipping the step is a misdemeanor for a register of deeds, with a fine up to $100, so the office does not bend on it.

sections.h2: How do Chippewa County homes measure up in the Census data?
sections.html:
By land area Chippewa is Michigan's second largest county, with 1,558 square miles of dry ground inside 2,698 total. It touches both Lake Huron and Lake Superior, and the Census puts density at only 23.6 residents per square mile.

The 2025 estimate is 36,081 people, down 1.9% from the 2020 base. Three of every four homes are owner-held (75.0%), and the middle rent is $797. A typical home is valued at $161,900, and a typical household takes in $62,217. The county has 20,556 housing units, and builders pulled 86 permits for them in 2025. In the 2020 count, 31.7% of units stood vacant and 27.5% of occupied homes were rented.

faqs.q: What is Chippewa County's price to record one deed?
faqs.a: The state fee under MCL 600.2567 is $30.00 a document whatever the page count. Add transfer tax where it applies and any certification charge the treasurer sets. The office at 906-635-6312 can quote the final total.

faqs.q: Can I search Chippewa County land records for free?
faqs.a: Yes. Guests can search the online index at no charge. A PDF of a document is $1.00 a page plus a $5.00 online fee per order, paid by credit card.

faqs.q: How far back do the Chippewa County records go?
faqs.a: The online indexes begin May 16, 1865. The system posts its own index range and upload date on its welcome screen, so you can see how current it is before you search.

faqs.q: Is a mortgage subject to transfer tax in Chippewa County?
faqs.a: No. MCL 207.505 exempts instruments given as security, and an assignment or discharge of them. You pay the recording fee, but not the transfer tax, when you record a mortgage.

faqs.q: Who handles a recording problem with a Chippewa County deed?
faqs.a: Reach the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, phone 906-635-6312, email rod@chippewacountymi.gov. A question about what the deed should say belongs with an attorney or the title agent.
